subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — transient scaling & burst terms for AuroraEdge
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@auroraedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@auroraedge.com>, Procurement <procure@auroraedge.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — expected peaks and burst windows

Ben —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams so we can close sizing and T&C:

1) Expected peaks: our internal telemetry shows a predictable daily peak between 15:00-18:00 PT with short spike events during product launches (roughly 10–20 minutes each) that can push token throughput ~2.5x above baseline. I've attached a CSV with measured qps and GPU-minutes from the last 30 days.

2) We need clarity on your burst model for Dedicated: how much headroom can we rely on (percentage over committed GPUs), how are preemptions handled, and what billing granularity applies to burst usage?

3) Autoscale policy: we run many short-lived interactive sessions; cold-start latency matters. Can you outline warm-up behavior and whether you support reserved warm workers for critical routes?

We are trying to finalize a reserved capacity commit by EOD next week. Please include an ops runbook and any SLA addenda for burst availability.

Best,
Lisa Chen\VP, Platform Engineering\AuroraEdge

[attachment: AuroraEdge_MeasuredPeak.csv (text/csv) — 12 KB]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — AuroraEdge (sizing + burst request)

Team — forwarding Lisa's note. Quick initial thoughts before we craft the reply to AuroraEdge and attach a concrete proposal: 

- Measured peaks look realistic; their 2.5x spike per launch matches observed customer patterns.
- Proposal outline: commit 40 A100-equivalent GPUs as baseline (predictable throughput) with a transient burst pool that can expand to 60 GPUs for up to 120 minutes per day aggregated, plus short 'micro-burst' headroom of +30% for sub-15-minute spikes.
- Billing: suggest we offer a two-tier burst charge: (a) micro-bursts (<=15 min) billed at 1.25x token rate, aggregated per-day; (b) extended burst minutes billed at standard reserved overage rate with min 5-minute billing increments. This keeps economics friendly for interactive spikes but lets us recoup ops cost for sustained uplift.
- Preemption & routing: micro-bursts served from ephemeral preemptible slab with automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model variant if preemption occurs. For extended bursts, favor non-preemptible shoulder pool where available.
- Warm-up: recommend a warm-reserve of ~8 hot workers pinned to their critical route (route-level pinning) to avoid cold KV-cache misses during spike start. Will include a canary ramp: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 90s for safety.

Action: Karthik, can you run quick cost calc for 40 commit + 20 transient GPUs with our standard reserved pricing and the above burst charge knobs? Lauren, please prepare an ops runbook skeleton (eviction behavior, fallback model mapping, alert thresholds) so we can attach it. I will draft the response and proposal PDF.

Thanks —
Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@auroraedge.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@auroraedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal & burst policy — AuroraEdge (RDW-2026-AE-47)

Lisa / Samir —

Thanks again for the data. Attached is our proposal PDF and a short ops runbook; summary below so you can skim quickly: 

Summary of recommended commitment:
- Baseline reserved: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs (region: us-west-2) — provides steady-state throughput and lower per-token unit cost.
- Transient burst pool: +20 GPUs (ephemeral) available for aggregated 120 minutes/day. Burst bank resets daily at 00:00 UTC.
- Micro-burst headroom: auto-expand up to +30% above current active allocation for spikes <=15 minutes (no per-minute provisioning required).

Billing & pricing mechanics:
- Baseline: standard reserved rate as quoted in the deal deck.
- Micro-bursts (<=15 minutes each): billed at 1.25x token unit rate, aggregated per day (free up to first 10 micro-burst minutes/day as courtesy during initial 60-day onboarding).
- Extended burst minutes (from transient pool): billed at 1.0x reserved overage rate with 5-minute billing increments.
- If transient pool is exhausted: automatic fallback to preemptible public slab (lower-cost compute) + optional model downgrade to a quantized variant (we will only do the downgrade after a 30s grace period and with explicit route-level config).

Operational controls & safety:
- Warm-reserve: we will pin 8 hot workers for your primary interactive route to reduce cold-starts and KV cache misses; these are part of the reserved commit.
- Canary ramp: standard 3-step ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over ~90s when new capacity is introduced to limit model cache churn.
- Eviction policy: preemptible slab uses LRU eviction by request age; we will not evict pinned warm workers.
- Monitoring & alerts: per-route 95th/99th latency alerts, token burn-rate alerts; automatic ops paging if burst bank consumed >70% within rolling 30-minute window.

Attachments: rdw-dedicated-burst-proposal-auroraedge-v1.pdf (proposal + SLO addendum), AuroraEdge_MeasuredPeak.csv (their telemetry).

If this aligns, we'll: (1) lock in the baseline + burst terms in the SOW; (2) produce a short SLA addendum that captures burst availability and failure modes; (3) schedule a 30-min runbook review with your SRE next week.

Ben Carter\Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal & burst policy — AuroraEdge (RDW-2026-AE-47)

Ben —

Appreciate the thoughtful proposal. A few quick items from procurement and infra: 

- The micro-burst courtesy 10 minutes/day during onboarding is acceptable. Please redact the onboarding clause and make it a 60-day trial period in the SOW.
- We want the fallback model downgrade to be opted-in per route (AuroraEdge will decide which routes can be downgraded). Please add an explicit route-config flag in the runbook.
- Can you add a short clause about billing visibility (daily burst usage report and per-minute breakdown for the first 14 days post-launch)?

Assuming those edits, procurement is comfortable moving to a signature-ready SOW. Let's schedule the runbook review for next Tue 10am PT.

—Samir
Head of SRE, AuroraEdge
